topic.angle: A 5000-year-old man preserved in an Alpine glacier and what he carried

body.claim: Ötzi, a man who lived in the 4th millennium BC, was found in 1991 with a copper axe, a quiver of 14 arrows and a dried tinder fungus.
body.why: He had been naturally preserved in glacier ice, so his body and belongings survived in the Ötztal Alps. He is Europe's oldest known natural human mummy, and his gear gives a rare view of Copper Age life.

probes.question: What was Ötzi's axe head made of?
Ötzi was found in the ____ Alps, on the Austria-Italy border.

image_brief.show: The Ötzi mummy on display at the South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology, or a replica of his copper axe

claims.claim: Claim: found in 1991 in the Ötztal Alps
claims.quote: Ötzi's remains were discovered on 19 September 1991 in the Ötztal Alps

claims.claim: Claim: lived in the 4th millennium BC
claims.quote: is the natural mummy of a man who lived during the 4th millennium BC

claims.claim: Claim: found with a copper axe and a quiver of 14 arrows
claims.quote: a copper axe with a yew handle, a chert -bladed knife with an ash handle and a quiver of 14 arrows

claims.claim: Claim: a dried fungus among his belongings
claims.quote: a bone awl and a dried fungus

claims.claim: Claim: the fungus was a tinder fungus
claims.quote: The other was a type of tinder fungus , included with part of what appeared to be a complex firelighting kit

claims.claim: Why: naturally preserved in glacier ice
claims.quote: he was a wet mummy that had been naturally preserved in glacier ice

claims.claim: Why: Europe's oldest known natural human mummy; view of Copper Age life
claims.quote: He is Europe's oldest known natural human mummy, showing an unprecedented view of Chalcolithic (Copper Age) Europeans

claims.claim: Probe 1: axe head almost pure copper
claims.quote: The 9.5-centimetre-long (3.7 in) axe head is almost pure copper

claims.claim: Probe 2: found in the Ötztal Alps on the Austria-Italy border
claims.quote: discovered on 19 September 1991 in the Ötztal Alps (hence the nickname "Ötzi") at the Austria-Italy border
